A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same rdFFT research. Text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison; pages 3–12 render identically. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original memory measurements, operator runtimes and numerical-error results in Tables 1–3. These establish original empirical results independently of the accuracy results attributed to BCA in Table 4.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original memory, runtime and numerical-error experiments in Tables 1–3. Retaining these results qualifies despite the absence of new experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same real-valued memory layout, in-place butterfly computations, inverse-transform procedure and circulant-training integration. The new PyTorch discussion note introduces no algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same single-layer and operator tests, GSM8K with LLaMA2-7B, and MRPC with RoBERTa-large. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged: standard FFT, rFFT, full fine-tuning and LoRA participate in the same respective comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains identical input dimensions, batch sizes, block sizes, model configurations, optimizer, precision, hardware and measurement procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The batch-size and block-size analyses, memory breakdown in Figure 2, and operator-size comparisons are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Table 3 still averages runtime over 1000 runs, and Section 5.2.2 retains the same statement about multiple random seeds for MRPC. Neither version adds seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–4 and Figure 2 are identical. For example, rdFFT's LLaMA2-7B peak memory at p=4096 remains 17.91 GB, and its forward operator runtime at that size remains 0.0687 ms.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Proposition 1 and its proof, and Equations 1–7 are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption or derivation is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about fully in-place real-domain FFT, bfloat16 support and training-memory savings. The added implementation-status note does not change these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of memory savings, synchronization-related runtime overhead and numerical fidelity are unchanged. Both retain the limitation that explicit complex-spectrum access requires conversion and additional memory.

D1.justification: V2 adds a paragraph after the introduction's contributions stating that upstreaming the operators into PyTorch is under discussion and pointing to issue 171022. V1 lacks this implementation-status and discussion-access information. The addition does not establish code availability or completed integration.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 25 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to existing FFT libraries and adaptation methods. The new implementation-discussion link does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a short implementation-status paragraph at the end of the introduction and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 2 tightens spacing between contribution bullets and slightly shifts the Related Works heading to accommodate the new paragraph. All figures, tables, captions and subsequent page layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new introduction paragraph provides implementation status and a specific pointer for following PyTorch integration discussions, modestly improving implementation traceability. This is a limited documentation benefit: the scientific exposition and evidence are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish runnable code availability or acceptance into PyTorch.
